Molecular weight, normal boiling point, Tc, Pc and acentric factor as given; standard liquid density: the saturated liquid at Tr = 0.7 (eq. 105, at the eq. 101 vapour pressure), because Tc lies below 288.7 K and no 60 F liquid exists; ideal-gas Cp eq. 16 (A=20754, B=0, C=0, D=0, E=0; data 10..1500 K) fitted by least squares as shifted_polynomial_5 over 115.78..900 K (33 points), largest deviation 0.000 % at 115.8 K, 0.000 % over 298.15..900 K; viscosity tables and freezing data in their entries. Imported by tools/compound-import.

fluid_domain.evidence: Fluid network only (not the column range): the ideal-gas Cp fit range, from max(ChemSep Cp data start, triple point) to 900 K; below it Cp is held and integrated, with a notice (a data-range end, never a validity floor). 100 Pa..2000000 Pa as the bundled light ends: PR78 from ChemSep critical constants, not qualified above that.

liquid.source: ChemSep v8.3 pure component data (Copyright (c) Harry Kooijman and Ross Taylor; Artistic License 2.0), as embedded in DWSIM 10.2.5 (DWSIM.Thermodynamics.dll resource chemsep1.xml), compound "Krypton" (ChemSep index 920, CAS 7439-90-9): liquid viscosity eq. 101 (A=-7.7422, B=-0.3975, C=-0.00054036, D=-9.2221e-8, E=2; data 119.75..129.25 K), sampled over max(data start, triple point) to 0.95 Tc into a log table by recursive bisection, log interpolation within 0.05 % at quarter and mid points. Past the data end, 129.25..198.93 K: estimated, ln(mu) linear in 1/T at the equation's slope at 129.25 K (Andrade form). No pressure correction; the parser continues the table past its ends.

henry_in_water.source: IAPWS G7-04, Guideline on the Henry's Constant and Vapor-Liquid Distribution Constant for Gases in H2O and D2O at High Temperatures (2004), after R. Fernandez-Prini, J. L. Alvarez, A. H. Harvey, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 32 (2003) 903, table of A, B, C for Kr in H2O: ln(kH/p*) = A/Tr + B tau^0.355/Tr + C Tr^-0.41 exp(tau), Tr = T/647.096 K, tau = 1 - Tr, p* the saturation pressure of water, kH on the mole-fraction basis. Coefficients as in Table 2 of the guideline. Copyright 2004 IAPWS; publication in whole or in part is allowed provided attribution is given to IAPWS.
